elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf"

elements.element: Paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: "to the extent paid up in full, are perpetual and irrevocable"

elements.element: Subscription/term licences terminable (revocable) only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: "are irrevocable during the term of this Agreement except in the case of an uncured material breach by the Company"
"may be transferred to any successor to the Company's business by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Affiliates covered (fallback conditions this on written notice)
elements.evidence: "extend to the Company's affiliates" — covered outright, i.e. without the notice condition, which is no worse for the Customer

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "any successor to the Company's business by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

reasons: All five atomic preferred elements are expressly present in the single inserted sentence: affiliate scope, contractor scope, perpetual-and-irrevocable paid-up rights, revocation limited to uncured material breach during the term, and transfer to a successor by merger/acquisition/asset sale.
The locked preferred target is achieved, so no reliance on the fallback bargain is needed; the fallback elements are also independently satisfied (affiliates covered, M&A successor transfer).

Minimality holds: the original clause had no licence-scope language at all, so a concise one-sentence insertion appended after the existing text is the least intrusive fix; no operative words of the hosting, bandwidth, or admin-tool commitments were altered or deleted.

Intent preserved: HDI's obligations in the first two sentences remain effective verbatim; the insertion uses only existing defined terms ("Company", "this Agreement", "Section 1.4") and introduces no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic.

Note (rationale only, not a deviation): the revocation carve-out is framed as "uncured material breach" without an express cure-period mechanic, and "affiliates" is not a defined term in the agreement — worth confirming in negotiation but neither shortfall defeats the preferred position.
